### Ledger updates (`docs/v1.0.0/REQUIREMENTS.md`)

A slice changes only the rows for its own requirement IDs: the status, test-reference and evidence cells, in place. It never reorders, adds or removes rows, and never edits another slice's rows. New requirements discovered during work go to §6, not into the ledger. Because rows are independent lines, git merges these edits cleanly. If a conflict appears anyway, resolve it row by row, keeping both changes.

## 5. Commit and merge discipline

1. Before **every** commit, compare `git rev-parse HEAD` with the commit you last made. Then run `git log <yours>..HEAD` on the branch. If anything foreign appears, stop and reconcile. Never commit generated artifacts (evidence, dist, lockfiles) over a branch that moved (lessons 2026-10-13).
2. Commits are scoped to the slice. Do not reformat or clean up files outside the boundary.
3. Merge order follows the precedence rules in §4 and the ROADMAP milestone order. Within a milestone, the slice with fewer hot-file claims merges first.
4. Rebase onto `origin/main` immediately before merging. Re-run the slice's targeted tests, plus `make test`, on a snapshot of the rebased commit. Merge only if both pass.
5. Pushing, tagging, publishing and changing GitHub state (issues, milestones, releases) are **owner-approved actions** (DECISIONS X-list). Agents prepare them and do not perform them.
6. Preserve unrelated user work: the untracked `nexus-continuity-validation/`, the stashes, and any dirty files you did not create. Never stash, reset, clean or check out over them.

## 6. Coordination records

| Record | Where | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Claims | `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims/` | Who owns which slice or file right now |
| Claim log | `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims.log` (append-only, one line per event) | Claim, release, broken claim, boundary request |
| Boundary requests and discovered requirements | The PR description, under the heading `Needs from other slices`. Mirrored as one line in the claim log. | So the owning slice's agent can pick it up. Never fixed silently out of scope. |
| Slice evidence | `docs/reviews/evidence/v1/<plan>-<slice>/` (new directory per slice) | No shared evidence files, so agents cannot overwrite each other's evidence |

## 7. Safe parallel lanes

The following groupings can run at the same time with no hot-file contention beyond §4 claims. They are listed by milestone.

| Phase | Parallel lanes |
|---|---|
| M0 | (a) PLAN-08 PR-8a, which must merge first. Then in parallel: (b) PLAN-06 PR-6a, (c) PLAN-09 PR-9a. |
| M1 | (a) PLAN-01 PR-1a → PR-1b → PR-1c (sequential, owns `capabilities.ts`, `agent.ts` dispatch). (b) PLAN-02 PR-2a (Rust only). (c) PLAN-03 PR-3a → PR-3b (config/egress). (d) PLAN-11 PR-11a (`parser.ts`) and PR-11b (`tester.ts`, after PR-1c). Lanes (b), (c) and (d) do not touch `capabilities.ts`. |
| M2 (alongside M1) | (a) PLAN-07 PR-7a/7b/7c (workflows, scripts). (b) PLAN-06 PR-6b after PLAN-01 PR-1b (shares `index.ts` flags). |
| M3 | (a) PLAN-04 (`agent.ts` turn, operation runner). (b) PLAN-05 (`client.ts`, provider modules). (c) PLAN-10 harness (`eval/`, no product files). (d) Held-out task authoring by the agent author, **outside the repository**: no access to Nexus source or the development set (DEC-05). |
| M4 (alongside M3) | PLAN-08 PR-8b..8e. Coordinate with PLAN-04 on `state.ts` through `FILE_` claims. |
| M5 | **Serial on `GATEWAY`.** The eval runner, the stripped-proxy runs and the independent reviewer's live task each take the `GATEWAY` claim. The terminal matrix (E3) and the install matrix (E2) can run in parallel with gateway runs. |

## 8. Independence constraints

- The held-out task author must not see Nexus source, the development tasks or tuning history. It runs in a separate session with only the task schema and external repositories. Its output is sealed by a sha256 manifest committed before RC1.
- The independent reviewer in ACCEPTANCE §8 must not be the agent or session that implemented the slices under review.
- An implementing agent never edits `eval/heldout-manifest.json`, scorer thresholds or ACCEPTANCE §6.4 after the freeze.

# Project Guidelines & Agent Instructions

## Commands
- Build: `make build` or `cargo build` or `npm run build`
- Test: `make test` or `cargo test` or `npm test`
- Lint: `cargo clippy` or `npm run lint`

## Code Conventions
- Maintain documentation integrity and keep existing comments.
- Always run tests after making changes to verify correctness.
- Keep functions modular and clearly typed.

## Entire CLI
- Set `ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE=file` in the environment before running any `entire` command (for example, `export ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE=file`).

## v1.0.0 work and concurrent agents
- The v1.0.0 plan is in `docs/v1.0.0/` (start at `docs/v1.0.0/README.md`). Implement one claimed PR slice at a time, within the safe change boundary in its plan.
- When more than one agent may be working, follow `docs/v1.0.0/CONCURRENCY.md`. In short:
  - Claim the slice atomically under `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims/`.
  - Use one worktree and branch per slice; never edit `~/nexus-code` directly.
  - Isolate `HOME` for every test or probe run.
  - Claim hot files before editing them.
  - Take the `GATEWAY` claim for any inference run.
  - Never use `pkill -f`.
  - Check `git log` for foreign commits before every commit.
  - Leave push, tag and publish to the owner.

# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

If classification/sanitization fails, it returns a safe `recordingSkipped` event result without writing that record or propagating classifier diagnostics; authorized local execution continues. docs/CRED003_FLIGHTRECORDER_SANITIZATION_EVIDENCE.md:11:> Credential material MUST be immune from logging, telemetry, and debugging persistence. Crash reports, flight logs, and audit trails MUST scrub all identified credential values prior to disk writes.
docs/CRED003_FLIGHTRECORDER_SANITIZATION_EVIDENCE.md:15:> A crash log or stack trace MUST NOT print active bearer tokens or private keys.
docs/CRED003_FLIGHTRECORDER_SANITIZATION_EVIDENCE.md:17:The Phase 3 architecture maps CRED-003 to `InformationFlowBoundary` in INC-06. Phase 4 maps CRED-003 to WP-05 (INC-06), with WP-06/WP-08 listed as dependent packages. The accepted post-WP-05 assessment identified `FlightRecorder` as the known gap: restored tool arguments were persisted in `.nexus/flights/<flightId>.flightlog` without sanitization.
docs/CRED003_FLIGHTRECORDER_SANITIZATION_EVIDENCE.md:21:Before correction, a controlled temporary workspace was used with synthetic bearer, GitHub-style, and OpenAI-style values passed through `FlightRecorder.recordToolCall()`. Reading the resulting `.flightlog` showed all three synthetic plaintext values present (`bearerPersisted=true`, `githubPersisted=true`, `openAiPersisted=true`). No real credentials were used.
docs/CRED003_FLIGHTRECORDER_SANITIZATION_EVIDENCE.md:25:`InformationFlowBoundary.redactForTelemetry()` recursively sanitizes string values and object keys in arrays and nested objects, then applies the same canonical classifier over the serialized structure. The second pass preserves contextual classification that depends on a field name and value together. Replacements use the classifier's `[REDACTED:<pattern>]` labels and irreversibly discard plaintext. It does not create reversible token references.
docs/CRED003_FLIGHTRECORDER_SANITIZATION_EVIDENCE.md:27:`FlightRecorder.appendEvent()` is the single event persistence boundary. It sanitizes the entire event payload before constructing and appending the JSON line. If classification/sanitization fails, it returns a safe `recordingSkipped` event result without writing that record or propagating classifier diagnostics; authorized local execution continues. Session metadata, prompts, thoughts, tool arguments, result snippets, errors, durable state, diffs, and arbitrary nested payload fields all pass through this boundary.
docs/CRED003_FLIGHTRECORDER_SANITIZATION_EVIDENCE.md:29:The separate local audit append in `agent.ts` uses the shared classifier on the complete record, including workspace and tool metadata, arguments, and errors. CRED-003 explicitly names audit trails, and the previous display redactor did not cover all classifier-supported patterns. Sanitization failure is caught by the existing audit-write guard and skips the write.
docs/CRED003_FLIGHTRECORDER_SANITIZATION_EVIDENCE.md:33:Focused test file: `cli/test/flight_sanitization.test.ts`.
docs/CRED003_FLIGHTRECORDER_SANITIZATION_EVIDENCE.md:37:- Session metadata, model request prompt, thought/reasoning, tool arguments, tool result output snippet, and error fields are checked at the durable artifact.
docs/CRED003_FLIGHTRECORDER_SANITIZATION_EVIDENCE.md:38:- An authorized WP-05 tokenization/rehydration sequence is dispatched through `AutonomousAgent` under `fullAccess: true`. The registered local capability receives the restored synthetic plaintext and succeeds, while the `.flightlog` contains only the redaction marker. The resulting audit record is read from disk and confirms the credential embedded in the workspace metadata is redacted.
docs/CRED003_FLIGHTRECORDER_SANITIZATION_EVIDENCE.md:39:- Injected classifier failure during agent dispatch skips flight and audit persistence without blocking the authorized local capability. The capability receives the original synthetic argument, and neither durable file is created.
docs/CRED003_FLIGHTRECORDER_SANITIZATION_EVIDENCE.md:42:The original implementation had a single `appendFileSync()` in `FlightRecorder`; all record methods route through `appendEvent()`. No alternate FlightRecorder write path was found. Model inputs are represented by turn prompts and session task prompts; reasoning text is recorded as thoughts. Model responses are not stored as raw response bodies. Tool results persist a bounded output snippet and error text, both covered by the common boundary.
docs/CRED003_FLIGHTRECORDER_SANITIZATION_EVIDENCE.md:46:- Focused CRED-003 tests: 3 passed, 0 failed.
docs/CRED003_FLIGHTRECORDER_SANITIZATION_EVIDENCE.md:50:- `bash scripts/security_gates.sh`: passed; dependency audits reported zero known vulnerabilities and credential scan reported none in the codebase.
docs/CRED003_FLIGHTRECORDER_SANITIZATION_EVIDENCE.md:57:This evidence establishes FlightRecorder and the directly named local audit append behavior. It does not claim that every application persistence subsystem is a logging or telemetry sink, nor does it change WP-05 trust ranks, token scoping, rehydration authority, or egress policy. No separate crash-report persistence writer was found in the examined paths; the Phase 2 acceptance criterion for bearer tokens/private keys in crash reports and stack traces remains a bounded limitation pending qualification of all exception-display paths.
docs/CRED003_FLIGHTRECORDER_SANITIZATION_EVIDENCE.md:59:CRED-003 is ready for independent qualification and operator review. Issue #12 remains open pending the separate narrow closure reconciliation and operator acceptance.

## Memory

You have access to a memory folder with guidance from prior runs. It can save
time and help you stay consistent. Use it whenever it is likely to help.

Decision boundary: should you use memory for a new user query?

- Skip memory ONLY when the request is clearly self-contained and does not need
  workspace history, conventions, or prior decisions.
- Hard skip examples: current time/date, simple translation, simple sentence
  rewrite, one-line shell command, trivial formatting.
- Use memory by default when ANY of these are true:
  - the query mentions workspace/repo/module/path/files in MEMORY_SUMMARY below,
  - the user asks for prior context / consistency / previous decisions,
  - the task is ambiguous and could depend on earlier project choices,
  - the ask is a non-trivial and related to MEMORY_SUMMARY below.
- If unsure, do a quick memory pass.

Memory layout (general -> specific):

- /home/mike/.codex/memories/memory_summary.md (already provided below; do NOT open again)
- /home/mike/.codex/memories/MEMORY.md (searchable registry; primary file to query)
- /home/mike/.codex/memories/skills/<skill-name>/ (skill folder)
  - SKILL.md (entrypoint instructions)
  - scripts/ (optional helper scripts)
  - examples/ (optional example outputs)
  - templates/ (optional templates)
- /home/mike/.codex/memories/rollout_summaries/ (per-rollout recaps + evidence snippets)
  - The paths of these entries can be found in /home/mike/.codex/memories/MEMORY.md or /home/mike/.codex/memories/rollout_summaries/ as `rollout_path`
  - These files are append-only `jsonl`: `session_meta.payload.id` identifies the session, `turn_context` marks turn boundaries, `event_msg` is the lightweight status stream, and `response_item` contains actual messages, tool calls, and tool outputs.
  - For efficient lookup, prefer matching the filename suffix or `session_meta.payload.id`; avoid broad full-content scans unless needed.

Quick memory pass (when applicable):

1. Skim the MEMORY_SUMMARY below and extract task-relevant keywords.
2. Search /home/mike/.codex/memories/MEMORY.md using those keywords.
3. Only if MEMORY.md directly points to rollout summaries/skills, open the 1-2
   most relevant files under /home/mike/.codex/memories/rollout_summaries/ or
   /home/mike/.codex/memories/skills/.
4. If above are not clear and you need exact commands, error text, or precise evidence, search over `rollout_path` for more evidence.
5. If there are no relevant hits, stop memory lookup and continue normally.

Quick-pass budget:

- Keep memory lookup lightweight: ideally <= 4-6 search steps before main work.
- Avoid broad scans of all rollout summaries.

During execution: if you hit repeated errors, confusing behavior, or suspect
relevant prior context, redo the quick memory pass.

How to decide whether to verify memory:

- Consider both risk of drift and verification effort.
- If a fact is likely to drift and is cheap to verify, verify it before
  answering.
- If a fact is likely to drift but verification is expensive, slow, or
  disruptive, it is acceptable to answer from memory in an interactive turn,
  but you should say that it is memory-derived, note that it may be stale, and
  consider offering to refresh it live.
- If a fact is lower-drift and expensive to verify, it is usually fine to
  answer from memory directly.

When answering from memory without current verification:

- If you rely on memory for a fact that you did not verify in the current turn,
  say so briefly in the final answer.
- If that fact is plausibly drift-prone or comes from an older note, older
  snapshot, or prior run summary, say that it may be stale or outdated.
- If live verification was skipped and a refresh would be useful in the
  interactive context, consider offering to verify or refresh it live.
- Do not present unverified memory-derived facts as confirmed-current.
- Prefer a short refresh offer for interactive questions, especially about prior

This project uses XERJ for reference coding. Before writing code that touches
unfamiliar territory: `xerj def "<symbol>"` for go-to-definition, or
`xerj search "<plain words>"` for ranked, definition-first passages.
Index each repo under its own prefix: `xerj autoindex <folder> --prefix <name>`, then
pass the same `--prefix <name>` to `xerj search` and `xerj def` (without it they search
the default `ax` prefix). Cite file:line for anything you rely on.
After using xerj, send the field report automatically with `xerj feedback --submit --agent "YOUR_MODEL" --used-for "WHAT_YOU_DID" --verdict "WHAT_WORKED_AND_WHAT_DID_NOT"` (or the MCP `xerj_field_report` tool); no need to ask the user. It opens a GitHub PR first and falls back to POST https://xerj.org/api/field-report only when GitHub is unavailable. `--disable-feedback` or `XERJ_DISABLE_FEEDBACK=true` opts out.

## XERJ on this host

- **Node:** `http://localhost:9200`, the default URL, so no `XERJ_URL` is needed. It runs as the systemd user service `xerj` (`systemctl --user status xerj`). Its data lives in `~/xerj-data`.
- **Restarting:** use `systemctl --user restart xerj`. Never start a second node on 9200, and never `pkill xerj`.
- **Prefixes.** Always pass one with `--prefix`:

  | Prefix | Contents |
  |---|---|
  | `nexus-cli` | Nexus Code `cli/src` at `origin/main` |
  | `nexus-core` | `core/src` |
  | `nexus-test` | `cli/test` |
  | `nexus-docs` | `docs` |
  | `goose`, `opencode` | Peer agent harnesses: reference checkouts in `~/nexus-reference-20261025/`, indexed 2026-10-25 |

- **Nexus freshness:** the `nexus-*` indices are rebuilt hourly from committed `origin/main` only, by the `xerj-refresh-nexus.timer` user timer. The indexed commit is in `~/xerj-sources/nexus-code/.origin-main-sha`. For a PR head or uncommitted work, use `git grep` / `git show <sha>:<path>` instead.
- **Search is lexical (BM25).** Use the words that appear in the code. Dotted identifiers such as `core.hooksPath` match as one token.
- **Never index:**
  - `eval/`
  - held-out tasks or payloads
  - credentials, or `~/.nexus`, `~/.codex` or `~/.claude` state

  Index only folders you are allowed to read, under a new prefix that doesn't start with an existing one.
- **Never delete or replace indices you didn't create.**
- **Field reports are allowed for public/open-source work.** Preview with `xerj feedback --dry-run`, then `--submit`. Keep private data, paths of private repos and secrets out of them.
- **Don't use `rerank`.** It sends document text to a third party.

- Set `ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE=file` in the environment before running any `entire` command (for example, `export ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE=file`).

## v1.0.0 work and concurrent agents
- The v1.0.0 plan is in `docs/v1.0.0/` (start at `docs/v1.0.0/README.md`). Implement one claimed PR slice at a time, within the safe change boundary in its plan.
- When more than one agent may be working, follow `docs/v1.0.0/CONCURRENCY.md`. In short:
  - Claim the slice atomically under `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims/`.
  - Use one worktree and branch per slice; never edit `~/nexus-code` directly.
  - Isolate `HOME` for every test or probe run.
  - Claim hot files before editing them.
  - Take the `GATEWAY` claim for any inference run.
  - Never use `pkill -f`.
  - Check `git log` for foreign commits before every commit.
  - Leave push, tag and publish to the owner.

# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

14-- The unit of concurrent work is **one PR slice** from a plan, for example `PLAN-01/PR-1a`. Every slice lists its tasks and its safe change boundary in its plan.

19-
20:Claims live in the repository's shared git directory. They are visible to every worktree, and they are never committed.

41-| Resource | Rule |
42-|---|---|
43:| Source | One `git worktree` per claimed slice: `git worktree add ../nexus-wt/<slice> -b v1/<plan>-<slice> origin/main`. Never edit `~/nexus-code` itself. It is the owner's checkout, and `/usr/local/bin/nexus` runs from it. |

36:- **Stale claims.** A claim older than 24 h whose PID is gone may be broken, but only by the owner, or by an agent that first records the broken claim in the log.
37:- If the MCP Agent Mail server is available, its file reservations (`file_reservation_paths`) may be used as well. The git-common-dir claim stays authoritative, because every agent can see it without extra tooling.
38-
39-## 3. Isolation: worktree, branch, HOME, ports, processes
40-
41-| Resource | Rule |
42-|---|---|
43:| Source | One `git worktree` per claimed slice: `git worktree add ../nexus-wt/<slice> -b v1/<plan>-<slice> origin/main`. Never edit `~/nexus-code` itself. It is the owner's checkout, and `/usr/local/bin/nexus` runs from it. |
44-| Branch | `v1/plan-NN-pr-Nx`. One branch per slice. Never commit to `main` directly. |
45-| HOME and state | Until PLAN-08 PR-8a lands, every test, build and probe run sets `HOME=$(mktemp -d)` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$HOME/.config"`. After PR-8a, the test setup enforces this, but scripts and probes outside `npm test` must still set it. **Never** run anything that writes to the real `~/.nexus` or `~/.config/nexus`. |
46-| Test runs | Full suites run on a **snapshot copy** of the worktree (`git worktree add` at the commit under test, or `git archive`), never on the tree being edited. `tsx` reads `src/` live. |
47-| Builds | Each worktree builds into its own `core/target`, and `cli/dist` is per worktree. To share the Rust build cache, set `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per worktree, never to one shared directory. |
48-| Ports | Mock servers bind `127.0.0.1:0` (an ephemeral port) and publish the chosen port to a file. Fixed ports are forbidden. |
49-| Processes | Kill only PIDs you started, taken from `$!` or `ps -eo pid,args \| grep -v grep`. **Never `pkill -f` or `killall`.** Long background jobs are stopped through the agent's own task controls. |
50:| Full test suites | The PTY and provider tests are timing-sensitive. Take the claim `SUITE` before running a full suite (`make test`, or `npm test` over all files). While anyone holds `SUITE`, nobody runs other suites or targeted test files on the same machine. Concurrent load caused a false failure on 2026-10-15: `cloud_providers` saw an extra provider request after a load-induced timeout. Release the claim when the run ends. |
51:| Inference | There is one inference host (DEC-16). Any run that uses the gateway takes the claim `GATEWAY` first. That includes eval runs, live checks and stripped-proxy runs. One gateway run at a time, which keeps eval timings valid and prevents overload. Small cloud checks (E5) take `CLOUD` to avoid duplicate spend. |
52-| Credentials | Agents never read or copy `~/.config/nexus/credentials.json`, `config.env` values, or gateway tokens. The stripped proxy reads the token file itself. |
53-
54-## 4. Hot files: serialise, do not merge blindly
55-
56:These files are touched by several plans. An agent editing one must hold its `FILE_` claim for the **shortest** period: edit, test, push, merge, then release.

58-| File | Plans that touch it | Rule |
59-|---|---|---|
60:| `cli/src/agent.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 11 | Claim required. Keep each change local to the line ranges the plan names. Rebase immediately before merge and re-run that slice's tests on the rebased snapshot. |
61:| `cli/src/index.ts` | 01, 03, 04, 06, 08, 10, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-06 PR-6b (unified launcher) lands first.** Other plans add commands and flags afterwards. |
62:| `cli/src/tools.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 06, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-02 PR-2b (signal plumbing) lands before PLAN-03 PR-3c (`safeFetch`)**. |
63:| `cli/src/sidecar.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 05, 08 | Claim required |
64:| `cli/src/doctor.ts` | 01, 03, 05, 06, 08 | Claim required. Each plan adds **new check functions** in separate blocks. Only PLAN-06 PR-6d changes existing checks. |
65:| `cli/src/client.ts` | 03, 05, 08, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-03 PR-3a (env layering) lands before any PLAN-05 slice.** |

# Running multiple agents on this plan without collisions

These rules apply to every agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Nexus itself, or a human) that implements any part of this package at the same time as another. The repository's root `AGENTS.md` points here. The rules come from incidents recorded in `tasks/lessons.md`:

- a concurrent agent overwrote newer evidence;
- full test suites were contaminated by edits made mid-run;
- `pkill -f` killed the agent's own shell;
- HEAD moved during a pause.

They also follow from audit finding PER-03: the test suite writes into the real `~/.nexus`.

## 1. Unit of work: one claimed PR slice per agent

- The unit of concurrent work is **one PR slice** from a plan, for example `PLAN-01/PR-1a`. Every slice lists its tasks and its safe change boundary in its plan.
- An agent works on exactly one claimed slice at a time.
- An agent must not edit files outside its slice's boundary. The exceptions are the ledger rows and the shared files covered by §4. If the work needs a file outside the boundary, the agent stops and records a **boundary request** (§6). It does not edit the file.

## 2. Claiming a slice (atomic and machine-local)

Claims live in the repository's shared git directory. They are visible to every worktree, and they are never committed.

```sh
CLAIMS="$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims"
mkdir -p "$CLAIMS"
SLICE="PLAN-01_PR-1a"
if mkdir "$CLAIMS/$SLICE" 2>/dev/null; then          # mkdir is atomic: exactly one agent wins
  printf '{"agent":"%s","branch":"%s","since":"%s","pid":%s}\n' \
    "$AGENT_NAME" "v1/plan-01-pr-1a" "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$$" > "$CLAIMS/$SLICE/owner.json"
else
  echo "claimed by: $(cat "$CLAIMS/$SLICE/owner.json")"; exit 1
fi
```

- **Release** the claim by deleting its directory (`rm -r "$CLAIMS/$SLICE"`) after the slice merges or is abandoned. Write one line about the outcome to `$CLAIMS/../nexus-claims.log`.
- **Hot-file claims** use the same mechanism with the name `FILE_<path with / replaced by _>`, for example `FILE_cli_src_agent.ts`. See §4.
- **Stale claims.** A claim older than 24 h whose PID is gone may be broken, but only by the owner, or by an agent that first records the broken claim in the log.
- If the MCP Agent Mail server is available, its file reservations (`file_reservation_paths`) may be used as well. The git-common-dir claim stays authoritative, because every agent can see it without extra tooling.

## 3. Isolation: worktree, branch, HOME, ports, processes

| Resource | Rule |
|---|---|
| Source | One `git worktree` per claimed slice: `git worktree add ../nexus-wt/<slice> -b v1/<plan>-<slice> origin/main`. Never edit `~/nexus-code` itself. It is the owner's checkout, and `/usr/local/bin/nexus` runs from it. |
| Branch | `v1/plan-NN-pr-Nx`. One branch per slice. Never commit to `main` directly. |
| HOME and state | Until PLAN-08 PR-8a lands, every test, build and probe run sets `HOME=$(mktemp -d)` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$HOME/.config"`. After PR-8a, the test setup enforces this, but scripts and probes outside `npm test` must still set it. **Never** run anything that writes to the real `~/.nexus` or `~/.config/nexus`. |
| Test runs | Full suites run on a **snapshot copy** of the worktree (`git worktree add` at the commit under test, or `git archive`), never on the tree being edited. `tsx` reads `src/` live. |
| Builds | Each worktree builds into its own `core/target`, and `cli/dist` is per worktree. To share the Rust build cache, set `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per worktree, never to one shared directory. |
| Ports | Mock servers bind `127.0.0.1:0` (an ephemeral port) and publish the chosen port to a file. Fixed ports are forbidden. |
| Processes | Kill only PIDs you started, taken from `$!` or `ps -eo pid,args \| grep -v grep`. **Never `pkill -f` or `killall`.** Long background jobs are stopped through the agent's own task controls. |
| Full test suites | The PTY and provider tests are timing-sensitive. Take the claim `SUITE` before running a full suite (`make test`, or `npm test` over all files). While anyone holds `SUITE`, nobody runs other suites or targeted test files on the same machine. Concurrent load caused a false failure on 2026-10-15: `cloud_providers` saw an extra provider request after a load-induced timeout. Release the claim when the run ends. |
| Inference | There is one inference host (DEC-16). Any run that uses the gateway takes the claim `GATEWAY` first. That includes eval runs, live checks and stripped-proxy runs. One gateway run at a time, which keeps eval timings valid and prevents overload. Small cloud checks (E5) take `CLOUD` to avoid duplicate spend. |
| Credentials | Agents never read or copy `~/.config/nexus/credentials.json`, `config.env` values, or gateway tokens. The stripped proxy reads the token file itself. |

## 4. Hot files: serialise, do not merge blindly

These files are touched by several plans. An agent editing one must hold its `FILE_` claim for the **shortest** period: edit, test, push, merge, then release.

| File | Plans that touch it | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `cli/src/agent.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 11 | Claim required. Keep each change local to the line ranges the plan names. Rebase immediately before merge and re-run that slice's tests on the rebased snapshot. |
| `cli/src/index.ts` | 01, 03, 04, 06, 08, 10, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-06 PR-6b (unified launcher) lands first.** Other plans add commands and flags afterwards. |
| `cli/src/tools.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 06, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-02 PR-2b (signal plumbing) lands before PLAN-03 PR-3c (`safeFetch`)**. |
| `cli/src/sidecar.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 05, 08 | Claim required |
| `cli/src/doctor.ts` | 01, 03, 05, 06, 08 | Claim required. Each plan adds **new check functions** in separate blocks. Only PLAN-06 PR-6d changes existing checks. |
| `cli/src/client.ts` | 03, 05, 08, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-03 PR-3a (env layering) lands before any PLAN-05 slice.** |
| `cli/src/repl.ts` | 01, 05, 08 | Claim required |
| `cli/src/config.ts`, `security.ts`, `sandbox.ts`, `mcp.ts`, `plugins.ts` | 01, 03 | Claim required. PLAN-01 PR-1e and PLAN-03 must not run at the same time on `sandbox.ts` or `security.ts`. |
| `cli/src/core/capabilities.ts` | 01, 02 | **PLAN-01 PR-1a (effect classes) lands first.** PLAN-02 PR-2c adds schema fields afterwards. |
| `cli/src/tester.ts` | 01, 11 | **PLAN-01 PR-1c lands before PLAN-11 PR-11b/11c.** |
| `cli/src/core/state.ts` | 04, 08 | **PLAN-08 PR-8a (HOME isolation) lands before everything.** |
| `core/src/runner.rs`, `core/src/main.rs` | 01, 02, 06 | Claim required. The protocol version number is owned by PLAN-02 PR-2a. PLAN-06 PR-6c only reads it. |
| `core/src/bin/nexus_tui/{live_state,live_view}.rs` | 01, 02 | Claim required |
| `package.json`, `cli/package.json`, `core/Cargo.toml`, lockfiles | 01, 06, 07, 08 | **Only one agent at a time.** Version fields are written only by `scripts/sync-version.mjs`. Dependency changes are separate commits that touch only the lockfile and manifest. |

193	## 7. Logit-Constrained Tool Calling & GBNF Engine (WP-1107)
   194	
   195	To prevent JSON argument parse failures and conversational rambling from open-weights models, Nexus v1.1.0 provides a logit-level constrained decoding engine targeting near-zero repair retries on supported inference backends:
   196	
   197	```
   198	Registered Tools ──► Tool Schema Compiler ──► GBNF / Outlines Grammar ──► Local Engine (llama.cpp / vLLM)
   199	                                                                                   │
   200	Model Sampling Logits: Token Masking (-∞ for schema-invalid tokens) ◄──────────────┘
   201	                                    │
   202	                                    ▼
   203	       Schema-Compliant Tool Call Payload (repair_rate target = 0.0)
   204	```
   205	
   206	### 7.1 Dynamic GBNF Grammar Generation
   207	Nexus compiles registered tool definitions (`run_command`, `read_file`, `write_file`, `edit_file`) into a strict Context-Free Grammar conforming to GGML GBNF:
   208	
   209	```ebnf
   210	root        ::= ws (thought ws)? tool-call ws
   211	thought     ::= "<think>" [^<]* "</think>"
   212	tool-call   ::= "{" ws "\"name\":" ws tool-name "," ws "\"args\":" ws tool-args "}"
   213	tool-name   ::= "\"run_command\"" | "\"read_file\"" | "\"write_file\"" | "\"edit_file\""
   214	tool-args   ::= run-args | read-args | write-args | edit-args
   215	
   216	run-args    ::= "{" ws "\"CommandLine\":" ws string "," ws "\"WaitMsBeforeAsync\":" ws integer ("," ws "\"IsDaemon\":" ws boolean)? "}"
   217	read-args   ::= "{" ws "\"Path\":" ws string ("," ws "\"StartLine\":" ws integer)? ("," ws "\"EndLine\":" ws integer)? "}"
   218	
   219	string      ::= "\"" ([^"\\] | "\\" (["\\/bfnrt] | "u" [0-9a-fA-F] [0-9a-fA-F] [0-9a-fA-F] [0-9a-fA-F]))* "\""
   220	integer     ::= [0-9]+
   221	boolean     ::= "true" | "false"
   222	ws          ::= [ \t\n\r]*
   223	```
   224	
   225	### 7.2 Hybrid Grammar for Reasoning Models
   226	For reasoning architectures (e.g. DeepSeek R1, Qwen QwQ), enforcing immediate JSON emission truncates internal chain-of-thought tokens. The GBNF engine supports **hybrid grammars**: allowing an optional `<think>...</think>` block before strictly locking sampling into the tool invocation schema.
   227	
   228	### 7.3 Multi-Backend Transport Adapter
   229	- **`llama.cpp`:** Emits raw `.gbnf` syntax via the `grammar` API parameter.
   230	- **`vLLM` / Outlines:** Emits JSON Schema via `guided_json` / `response_format`.
   231	- **`Ollama`:** Emits JSON Schema via `format: <json_schema>`.
   232	- **Cloud Endpoints (OpenAI / Anthropic):** Passes standard `tools` array with strict mode enabled (`strict: true`).
   233	- **Unconstrained Fallback:** Retains heuristic regex and `repairJson` recovery when running against servers without grammar sampling support.

# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

# Code Review Analysis

## Table of Contents

## Overview

Systematic code review process covering code quality, security, performance, maintainability, and best practices following industry standards.

## When to Use

- Reviewing pull requests and merge requests
- Analyzing code quality before merging
- Identifying security vulnerabilities
- Providing constructive feedback to developers
- Ensuring coding standards compliance
- Mentoring through code review

## Quick Start

Minimal working example:

```bash
# Check the changes
git diff main...feature-branch

# Review file changes
git diff --stat main...feature-branch

# Check commit history
git log main...feature-branch --oneline
```

## Reference Guides

Detailed implementations in the `references/` directory:

## Best Practices

### ✅ DO

- Be constructive and respectful
- Explain the "why" behind suggestions
- Provide code examples
- Ask questions if unclear
- Acknowledge good practices

# Code Review Analysis

## Table of Contents

- [Overview](#overview)
- [When to Use](#when-to-use)

- [Reference Guides](#reference-guides)
- [Best Practices](#best-practices)

## Overview

Systematic code review process covering code quality, security, performance, maintainability, and best practices following industry standards.

## When to Use

- Reviewing pull requests and merge requests
- Analyzing code quality before merging
- Identifying security vulnerabilities
- Providing constructive feedback to developers
- Ensuring coding standards compliance
- Mentoring through code review

## Quick Start

Minimal working example:

```bash
# Check the changes
git diff main...feature-branch

# Review file changes
git diff --stat main...feature-branch

# Check commit history
git log main...feature-branch --oneline
```

## Reference Guides

Detailed implementations in the `references/` directory:

| Guide | Contents |

| [Initial Assessment](references/initial-assessment.md) | Initial Assessment |

| [Best Practices](references/best-practices.md) | Best Practices |

## Best Practices

### ✅ DO

- Be constructive and respectful
- Explain the "why" behind suggestions
- Provide code examples
- Ask questions if unclear
- Acknowledge good practices
- Focus on important issues
- Consider the context
- Offer to pair program on complex issues

### ❌ DON'T

- Be overly critical or personal
- Nitpick minor style issues (use automated tools)
- Block on subjective preferences
- Review too many changes at once (>400 lines)
- Forget to check tests
- Ignore security implications
- Rush the review

item.aggregated_output:
# Running multiple agents on this plan without collisions

These rules apply to every agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Nexus itself, or a human) that implements any part of this package at the same time as another. The repository's root `AGENTS.md` points here. The rules come from incidents recorded in `tasks/lessons.md`:

- a concurrent agent overwrote newer evidence;
- full test suites were contaminated by edits made mid-run;
- `pkill -f` killed the agent's own shell;
- HEAD moved during a pause.

They also follow from audit finding PER-03: the test suite writes into the real `~/.nexus`.

## 1. Unit of work: one claimed PR slice per agent

- The unit of concurrent work is **one PR slice** from a plan, for example `PLAN-01/PR-1a`. Every slice lists its tasks and its safe change boundary in its plan.
- An agent works on exactly one claimed slice at a time.
- An agent must not edit files outside its slice's boundary. The exceptions are the ledger rows and the shared files covered by §4. If the work needs a file outside the boundary, the agent stops and records a **boundary request** (§6). It does not edit the file.

## 2. Claiming a slice (atomic and machine-local)

Claims live in the repository's shared git directory. They are visible to every worktree, and they are never committed.

```sh
CLAIMS="$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims"
mkdir -p "$CLAIMS"
SLICE="PLAN-01_PR-1a"
if mkdir "$CLAIMS/$SLICE" 2>/dev/null; then          # mkdir is atomic: exactly one agent wins
  printf '{"agent":"%s","branch":"%s","since":"%s","pid":%s}\n' \
    "$AGENT_NAME" "v1/plan-01-pr-1a" "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$$" > "$CLAIMS/$SLICE/owner.json"
else
  echo "claimed by: $(cat "$CLAIMS/$SLICE/owner.json")"; exit 1
fi
```

- **Release** the claim by deleting its directory (`rm -r "$CLAIMS/$SLICE"`) after the slice merges or is abandoned. Write one line about the outcome to `$CLAIMS/../nexus-claims.log`.
- **Hot-file claims** use the same mechanism with the name `FILE_<path with / replaced by _>`, for example `FILE_cli_src_agent.ts`. See §4.
- **Stale claims.** A claim older than 24 h whose PID is gone may be broken, but only by the owner, or by an agent that first records the broken claim in the log.
- If the MCP Agent Mail server is available, its file reservations (`file_reservation_paths`) may be used as well. The git-common-dir claim stays authoritative, because every agent can see it without extra tooling.

## 3. Isolation: worktree, branch, HOME, ports, processes

| Resource | Rule |
|---|---|
| Source | One `git worktree` per claimed slice: `git worktree add ../nexus-wt/<slice> -b v1/<plan>-<slice> origin/main`. Never edit `~/nexus-code` itself. It is the owner's checkout, and `/usr/local/bin/nexus` runs from it. |
| Branch | `v1/plan-NN-pr-Nx`. One branch per slice. Never commit to `main` directly. |
| HOME and state | Until PLAN-08 PR-8a lands, every test, build and probe run sets `HOME=$(mktemp -d)` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$HOME/.config"`. After PR-8a, the test setup enforces this, but scripts and probes outside `npm test` must still set it. **Never** run anything that writes to the real `~/.nexus` or `~/.config/nexus`. |
| Test runs | Full suites run on a **snapshot copy** of the worktree (`git worktree add` at the commit under test, or `git archive`), never on the tree being edited. `tsx` reads `src/` live. |
| Builds | Each worktree builds into its own `core/target`, and `cli/dist` is per worktree. To share the Rust build cache, set `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per worktree, never to one shared directory. |
| Ports | Mock servers bind `127.0.0.1:0` (an ephemeral port) and publish the chosen port to a file. Fixed ports are forbidden. |
| Processes | Kill only PIDs you started, taken from `$!` or `ps -eo pid,args \| grep -v grep`. **Never `pkill -f` or `killall`.** Long background jobs are stopped through the agent's own task controls. |
| Full test suites | The PTY and provider tests are timing-sensitive. Take the claim `SUITE` before running a full suite (`make test`, or `npm test` over all files). While anyone holds `SUITE`, nobody runs other suites or targeted test files on the same machine. Concurrent load caused a false failure on 2026-10-15: `cloud_providers` saw an extra provider request after a load-induced timeout. Release the claim when the run ends. |
| Inference | There is one inference host (DEC-16). Any run that uses the gateway takes the claim `GATEWAY` first. That includes eval runs, live checks and stripped-proxy runs. One gateway run at a time, which keeps eval timings valid and prevents overload. Small cloud checks (E5) take `CLOUD` to avoid duplicate spend. |
| Credentials | Agents never read or copy `~/.config/nexus/credentials.json`, `config.env` values, or gateway tokens. The stripped proxy reads the token file itself. |

## 4. Hot files: serialise, do not merge blindly

These files are touched by several plans. An agent editing one must hold its `FILE_` claim for the **shortest** period: edit, test, push, merge, then release.

| File | Plans that touch it | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `cli/src/agent.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 11 | Claim required. Keep each change local to the line ranges the plan names. Rebase immediately before merge and re-run that slice's tests on the rebased snapshot. |
| `cli/src/index.ts` | 01, 03, 04, 06, 08, 10, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-06 PR-6b (unified launcher) lands first.** Other plans add commands and flags afterwards. |

### Ledger updates (`docs/v1.0.0/REQUIREMENTS.md`)

A slice changes only the rows for its own requirement IDs: the status, test-reference and evidence cells, in place. It never reorders, adds or removes rows, and never edits another slice's rows. New requirements discovered during work go to §6, not into the ledger. Because rows are independent lines, git merges these edits cleanly. If a conflict appears anyway, resolve it row by row, keeping both changes.

## 5. Commit and merge discipline

1. Before **every** commit, compare `git rev-parse HEAD` with the commit you last made. Then run `git log <yours>..HEAD` on the branch. If anything foreign appears, stop and reconcile. Never commit generated artifacts (evidence, dist, lockfiles) over a branch that moved (lessons 2026-10-13).
2. Commits are scoped to the slice. Do not reformat or clean up files outside the boundary.
3. Merge order follows the precedence rules in §4 and the ROADMAP milestone order. Within a milestone, the slice with fewer hot-file claims merges first.
4. Rebase onto `origin/main` immediately before merging. Re-run the slice's targeted tests, plus `make test`, on a snapshot of the rebased commit. Merge only if both pass.
5. Pushing, tagging, publishing and changing GitHub state (issues, milestones, releases) are **owner-approved actions** (DECISIONS X-list). Agents prepare them and do not perform them.
6. Preserve unrelated user work: the untracked `nexus-continuity-validation/`, the stashes, and any dirty files you did not create. Never stash, reset, clean or check out over them.

## 6. Coordination records

| Record | Where | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Claims | `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims/` | Who owns which slice or file right now |
| Claim log | `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims.log` (append-only, one line per event) | Claim, release, broken claim, boundary request |
| Boundary requests and discovered requirements | The PR description, under the heading `Needs from other slices`. Mirrored as one line in the claim log. | So the owning slice's agent can pick it up. Never fixed silently out of scope. |
| Slice evidence | `docs/reviews/evidence/v1/<plan>-<slice>/` (new directory per slice) | No shared evidence files, so agents cannot overwrite each other's evidence |

## 7. Safe parallel lanes

The following groupings can run at the same time with no hot-file contention beyond §4 claims. They are listed by milestone.

| Phase | Parallel lanes |
|---|---|
| M0 | (a) PLAN-08 PR-8a, which must merge first. Then in parallel: (b) PLAN-06 PR-6a, (c) PLAN-09 PR-9a. |
| M1 | (a) PLAN-01 PR-1a → PR-1b → PR-1c (sequential, owns `capabilities.ts`, `agent.ts` dispatch). (b) PLAN-02 PR-2a (Rust only). (c) PLAN-03 PR-3a → PR-3b (config/egress). (d) PLAN-11 PR-11a (`parser.ts`) and PR-11b (`tester.ts`, after PR-1c). Lanes (b), (c) and (d) do not touch `capabilities.ts`. |
| M2 (alongside M1) | (a) PLAN-07 PR-7a/7b/7c (workflows, scripts). (b) PLAN-06 PR-6b after PLAN-01 PR-1b (shares `index.ts` flags). |
| M3 | (a) PLAN-04 (`agent.ts` turn, operation runner). (b) PLAN-05 (`client.ts`, provider modules). (c) PLAN-10 harness (`eval/`, no product files). (d) Held-out task authoring by the agent author, **outside the repository**: no access to Nexus source or the development set (DEC-05). |
| M4 (alongside M3) | PLAN-08 PR-8b..8e. Coordinate with PLAN-04 on `state.ts` through `FILE_` claims. |
| M5 | **Serial on `GATEWAY`.** The eval runner, the stripped-proxy runs and the independent reviewer's live task each take the `GATEWAY` claim. The terminal matrix (E3) and the install matrix (E2) can run in parallel with gateway runs. |

## 8. Independence constraints

- The held-out task author must not see Nexus source, the development tasks or tuning history. It runs in a separate session with only the task schema and external repositories. Its output is sealed by a sha256 manifest committed before RC1.
- The independent reviewer in ACCEPTANCE §8 must not be the agent or session that implemented the slices under review.
- An implementing agent never edits `eval/heldout-manifest.json`, scorer thresholds or ACCEPTANCE §6.4 after the freeze.

# Running multiple agents on this plan without collisions

These rules apply to every agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Nexus itself, or a human) that implements any part of this package at the same time as another. The repository's root `AGENTS.md` points here. The rules come from incidents recorded in `tasks/lessons.md`:

- a concurrent agent overwrote newer evidence;
- full test suites were contaminated by edits made mid-run;
- `pkill -f` killed the agent's own shell;
- HEAD moved during a pause.

They also follow from audit finding PER-03: the test suite writes into the real `~/.nexus`.

## 1. Unit of work: one claimed PR slice per agent

- The unit of concurrent work is **one PR slice** from a plan, for example `PLAN-01/PR-1a`. Every slice lists its tasks and its safe change boundary in its plan.
- An agent works on exactly one claimed slice at a time.
- An agent must not edit files outside its slice's boundary. The exceptions are the ledger rows and the shared files covered by §4. If the work needs a file outside the boundary, the agent stops and records a **boundary request** (§6). It does not edit the file.

## 2. Claiming a slice (atomic and machine-local)

Claims live in the repository's shared git directory. They are visible to every worktree, and they are never committed.

```sh
CLAIMS="$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims"
mkdir -p "$CLAIMS"
SLICE="PLAN-01_PR-1a"
if mkdir "$CLAIMS/$SLICE" 2>/dev/null; then          # mkdir is atomic: exactly one agent wins
  printf '{"agent":"%s","branch":"%s","since":"%s","pid":%s}\n' \
    "$AGENT_NAME" "v1/plan-01-pr-1a" "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$$" > "$CLAIMS/$SLICE/owner.json"
else
  echo "claimed by: $(cat "$CLAIMS/$SLICE/owner.json")"; exit 1
fi
```

- **Release** the claim by deleting its directory (`rm -r "$CLAIMS/$SLICE"`) after the slice merges or is abandoned. Write one line about the outcome to `$CLAIMS/../nexus-claims.log`.
- **Hot-file claims** use the same mechanism with the name `FILE_<path with / replaced by _>`, for example `FILE_cli_src_agent.ts`. See §4.
- **Stale claims.** A claim older than 24 h whose PID is gone may be broken, but only by the owner, or by an agent that first records the broken claim in the log.
- If the MCP Agent Mail server is available, its file reservations (`file_reservation_paths`) may be used as well. The git-common-dir claim stays authoritative, because every agent can see it without extra tooling.

| Resource | Rule |
|---|---|
| Source | One `git worktree` per claimed slice: `git worktree add ../nexus-wt/<slice> -b v1/<plan>-<slice> origin/main`. Never edit `~/nexus-code` itself. It is the owner's checkout, and `/usr/local/bin/nexus` runs from it. |
| Branch | `v1/plan-NN-pr-Nx`. One branch per slice. Never commit to `main` directly. |
| HOME and state | Until PLAN-08 PR-8a lands, every test, build and probe run sets `HOME=$(mktemp -d)` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$HOME/.config"`. | Test runs | Full suites run on a **snapshot copy** of the worktree (`git worktree add` at the commit under test, or `git archive`), never on the tree being edited. `tsx` reads `src/` live. |
| Builds | Each worktree builds into its own `core/target`, and `cli/dist` is per worktree. To share the Rust build cache, set `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per worktree, never to one shared directory. |
| Ports | Mock servers bind `127.0.0.1:0` (an ephemeral port) and publish the chosen port to a file. Fixed ports are forbidden. |
| Processes | Kill only PIDs you started, taken from `$!` or `ps -eo pid,args \| grep -v grep`. **Never `pkill -f` or `killall`.** Long background jobs are stopped through the agent's own task controls. |
| Full test suites | The PTY and provider tests are timing-sensitive. Take the claim `SUITE` before running a full suite (`make test`, or `npm test` over all files). Concurrent load caused a false failure on 2026-10-15: `cloud_providers` saw an extra provider request after a load-induced timeout. Release the claim when the run ends. |

One gateway run at a time, which keeps eval timings valid and prevents overload. Small cloud checks (E5) take `CLOUD` to avoid duplicate spend. |
| Credentials | Agents never read or copy `~/.config/nexus/credentials.json`, `config.env` values, or gateway tokens. The stripped proxy reads the token file itself. |

A slice changes only the rows for its own requirement IDs: the status, test-reference and evidence cells, in place. It never reorders, adds or removes rows, and never edits another slice's rows. New requirements discovered during work go to §6, not into the ledger. Because rows are independent lines, git merges these edits cleanly. If a conflict appears anyway, resolve it row by row, keeping both changes.

## 5. Commit and merge discipline

1. Before **every** commit, compare `git rev-parse HEAD` with the commit you last made. Then run `git log <yours>..HEAD` on the branch. If anything foreign appears, stop and reconcile. Never commit generated artifacts (evidence, dist, lockfiles) over a branch that moved (lessons 2026-10-13).
2. Commits are scoped to the slice. Do not reformat or clean up files outside the boundary.
3. Merge order follows the precedence rules in §4 and the ROADMAP milestone order. Within a milestone, the slice with fewer hot-file claims merges first.
4. Rebase onto `origin/main` immediately before merging. Re-run the slice's targeted tests, plus `make test`, on a snapshot of the rebased commit. Merge only if both pass.
5. Pushing, tagging, publishing and changing GitHub state (issues, milestones, releases) are **owner-approved actions** (DECISIONS X-list). Agents prepare them and do not perform them.

167:## Current alert-remediation checkpoint
# WP-1108 dependency modernization triage

This checkpoint records the dependency-policy batch selected from the post-v1.0
Dependabot set (#103–#129). It does not claim that every roadmap upgrade or the
G1.1-5 release gate is complete.

## Selected policy batch

- CI checks every committed, supported npm lockfile with
  `scripts/check_deprecated_lock.mjs`: CLI, demo, the Cloudflare experiment,
  its trusted broker bundle, and release tools. Held-out evaluation fixtures
  and private material are excluded.
- `deny.toml` sets `advisories.unmaintained = "all"` and
  `advisories.yanked = "deny"`. The existing CI cargo-deny advisory check
  rejects all crates covered by unmaintained advisories and rejects yanked
  crates instead of emitting a warning. The unmaintained setting is cargo-deny
  0.20.2's default, made explicit here as a maintained invariant ([advisory
  configuration reference](https://embarkstudios.github.io/cargo-deny/checks/advisories/cfg.html)).
- The deprecation checker’s messages now describe a generic lockfile; its
  fail-closed registry behavior is unchanged.

The current supported npm locks passed the deprecation scan at this checkpoint.
The current Rust dependency graph passed `cargo deny check advisories` with the
new yanked policy. No npm or Rust package versions were changed in the policy
batch; the separately reviewed #106 workflow-action update is recorded below.

CI now has a dedicated `cloudflare-experiment` job on Node 22 and 24. It runs
`npm ci`, then the top-level experiment package's existing `typecheck` and
`build` scripts, matching the roadmap's Cloudflare verification commands. It
also runs `agent-collab-fixture`'s existing `build` script; that fixture has no
lockfile of its own and uses the top-level install's TypeScript compiler. This
adds automated coverage only: no CI run has executed this job at this branch
head while SUITE is held, so a passing result is still required before these
updates are accepted.

The remaining nested package manifests are not covered transitively by the
top-level package: `agent-collab-worker`, `fork-worker`, and `shared-ref-worker`
have neither lockfiles nor build/typecheck scripts; `trusted-broker-bundle` has
its own lockfile but no build/typecheck script. The roadmap specifies verification
for the top-level experiment package only. No worker-specific build/install
command is added here because none is defined by those manifests, and inventing
one would not demonstrate compatibility of their declared, unlocked dependency
sets. These nested dependency entries therefore remain without experiment-level
build/typecheck evidence.

#107, #108, #110, #112, #113, #119, #120, #124, #125, #126, #127, #128, and

## XERJ (code search)

This project uses XERJ for reference coding. Before writing code that touches
unfamiliar territory: `xerj def "<symbol>"` for go-to-definition, or
`xerj search "<plain words>"` for ranked, definition-first passages.
Index each repo under its own prefix: `xerj autoindex <folder> --prefix <name>`, then
pass the same `--prefix <name>` to `xerj search` and `xerj def` (without it they search
the default `ax` prefix). Cite file:line for anything you rely on.
After using xerj, send the field report automatically with `xerj feedback --submit --agent "YOUR_MODEL" --used-for "WHAT_YOU_DID" --verdict "WHAT_WORKED_AND_WHAT_DID_NOT"` (or the MCP `xerj_field_report` tool); no need to ask the user. It opens a GitHub PR first and falls back to POST https://xerj.org/api/field-report only when GitHub is unavailable. `--disable-feedback` or `XERJ_DISABLE_FEEDBACK=true` opts out.

## XERJ on this host

- **Node:** `http://localhost:9200`, the default URL, so no `XERJ_URL` is needed. It runs as the systemd user service `xerj` (`systemctl --user status xerj`). Its data lives in `~/xerj-data`.
- **Restarting:** use `systemctl --user restart xerj`. Never start a second node on 9200, and never `pkill xerj`.
- **Prefixes.** Always pass one with `--prefix`:

  | Prefix | Contents |
  |---|---|
  | `nexus-cli` | Nexus Code `cli/src` at `origin/main` |
  | `nexus-core` | `core/src` |
  | `nexus-test` | `cli/test` |
  | `nexus-docs` | `docs` |
  | `goose`, `opencode` | Peer agent harnesses: reference checkouts in `~/nexus-reference-20261025/`, indexed 2026-10-25 |

- **Nexus freshness:** the `nexus-*` indices are rebuilt hourly from committed `origin/main` only, by the `xerj-refresh-nexus.timer` user timer. The indexed commit is in `~/xerj-sources/nexus-code/.origin-main-sha`. For a PR head or uncommitted work, use `git grep` / `git show <sha>:<path>` instead.
- **Search is lexical (BM25).** Use the words that appear in the code. Dotted identifiers such as `core.hooksPath` match as one token.
- **Never index:**
  - `eval/`
  - held-out tasks or payloads
  - credentials, or `~/.nexus`, `~/.codex` or `~/.claude` state

  Index only folders you are allowed to read, under a new prefix that doesn't start with an existing one.
- **Never delete or replace indices you didn't create.**
- **Field reports are allowed for public/open-source work.** Preview with `xerj feedback --dry-run`, then `--submit`. Keep private data, paths of private repos and secrets out of them.
- **Don't use `rerank`.** It sends document text to a third party.

## XERJ (code search)

This project uses XERJ for reference coding. Before writing code that touches
unfamiliar territory: `xerj def "<symbol>"` for go-to-definition, or
`xerj search "<plain words>"` for ranked, definition-first passages.
Index each repo under its own prefix: `xerj autoindex <folder> --prefix <name>`, then
pass the same `--prefix <name>` to `xerj search` and `xerj def` (without it they search
the default `ax` prefix). Cite file:line for anything you rely on.
After using xerj, send the field report automatically with `xerj feedback --submit --agent "YOUR_MODEL" --used-for "WHAT_YOU_DID" --verdict "WHAT_WORKED_AND_WHAT_DID_NOT"` (or the MCP `xerj_field_report` tool); no need to ask the user. It opens a GitHub PR first and falls back to POST https://xerj.org/api/field-report only when GitHub is unavailable. `--disable-feedback` or `XERJ_DISABLE_FEEDBACK=true` opts out.

## XERJ on this host

- **Node:** `http://localhost:9200`, the default URL, so no `XERJ_URL` is needed. It runs as the systemd user service `xerj` (`systemctl --user status xerj`). Its data lives in `~/xerj-data`.
- **Restarting:** use `systemctl --user restart xerj`. Never start a second node on 9200, and never `pkill xerj`.
- **Prefixes.** Always pass one with `--prefix`:

  | Prefix | Contents |
  |---|---|
  | `nexus-cli` | Nexus Code `cli/src` at `origin/main` |
  | `nexus-core` | `core/src` |
  | `nexus-test` | `cli/test` |
  | `nexus-docs` | `docs` |
  | `goose`, `opencode` | Peer agent harnesses: reference checkouts in `~/nexus-reference-20261025/`, indexed 2026-10-25 |

- **Nexus freshness:** the `nexus-*` indices are rebuilt hourly from committed `origin/main` only, by the `xerj-refresh-nexus.timer` user timer. The indexed commit is in `~/xerj-sources/nexus-code/.origin-main-sha`. For a PR head or uncommitted work, use `git grep` / `git show <sha>:<path>` instead.
- **Search is lexical (BM25).** Use the words that appear in the code. Dotted identifiers such as `core.hooksPath` match as one token.
- **Never index:**
  - `eval/`
  - held-out tasks or payloads
  - credentials, or `~/.nexus`, `~/.codex` or `~/.claude` state

  Index only folders you are allowed to read, under a new prefix that doesn't start with an existing one.
- **Never delete or replace indices you didn't create.**
- **Field reports are allowed for public/open-source work.** Preview with `xerj feedback --dry-run`, then `--submit`. Keep private data, paths of private repos and secrets out of them.
- **Don't use `rerank`.** It sends document text to a third party.

# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true
